claims.title: analyze runs analysis over the current repository
claims.claim: Running `truecourse analyze` inside a repository runs static and LLM analysis over that repository and reports the violations it found.
claims.verifyVia: combination: exit code 0 and stdout summarizing the analysis of the current repo

claims.title: results are stored as plain JSON under .truecourse/
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze` stores its results as plain JSON files under `.truecourse/` in the analyzed repository.
claims.verifyVia: file: `.truecourse/` exists after the run and contains parseable JSON result files

claims.title: analyze runs the full analysis in-process
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze` runs the full analysis in-process, so it completes with no dashboard or other TrueCourse process running.
claims.verifyVia: exit-code: analyze exits 0 with no server started beforehand

claims.title: list shows the violations analyze found
claims.claim: After an analysis, `truecourse list` prints the violations that analysis found.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: violation rows from the latest analysis

claims.title: analyze --diff diffs the working tree against a committed baseline
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --diff` diffs the working tree against a committed baseline.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: diff output that references the committed baseline rather than the full violation set

claims.title: analyze catches architecture problems
claims.claim: Analysis reports Architecture-category violations such as circular dependencies, layer violations, god modules, dead modules, tight coupling, and cross-service imports.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Architecture-category violation for code containing one of the listed patterns

claims.title: analyze catches code-quality problems

claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Code quality violation for code containing one of the listed patterns

claims.title: analyze catches security problems
claims.claim: Analysis reports Security violations such as SQL injection, hardcoded secrets, eval usage, insecure random, XSS, path traversal, and unsafe deserialization.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Security violation for code containing one of the listed patterns

claims.title: analyze catches bugs
claims.claim: Analysis reports Bugs-category violations such as race conditions, type mismatches, mutable defaults, implicit optional, off-by-one, and unchecked returns.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Bugs violation for code containing one of the listed patterns

claims.title: analyze catches performance problems
claims.claim: Analysis reports Performance violations such as N+1 queries, O(n^2) string concatenation, unnecessary allocations, missing pagination, and sync I/O in async code.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Performance violation for code containing one of the listed patterns

claims.title: analyze catches reliability problems
claims.claim: Analysis reports Reliability violations such as unhandled promises, resource leaks, missing timeouts, swallowed exceptions, and unsafe error handling.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Reliability violation for code containing one of the listed patterns

claims.title: analyze catches database problems
claims.claim: Analysis reports Database violations such as missing indexes, missing transactions, lazy loading in loops, raw SQL bypassing the ORM, and schema issues.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Database violation for code containing one of the listed patterns

claims.title: analyze catches style problems
claims.claim: Analysis reports Style violations such as import ordering, naming conventions, docstring completeness, and formatting preferences.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: `truecourse list` shows at least one Style violation for code containing one of the listed patterns

claims.title: ships 1,500+ deterministic rules and 100 LLM rules

claims.verifyVia: stdout: the rule inventory printed by `truecourse rules list` totals over 1,500 deterministic and 100 LLM rules

claims.title: deterministic rules cost nothing and make no API calls
claims.claim: Deterministic rules make no API calls and cost nothing, so an analysis without LLM rules completes with zero LLM calls and zero cost.
claims.verifyVia: combination: `truecourse analyze --no-llm` exits 0 with no LLM transport configured, and stdout reports no LLM calls or cost

claims.title: LLM rules send source code to the configured LLM

claims.verifyVia: stdout: an analysis run with LLM rules enabled reports LLM calls / token usage against the configured transport

claims.title: LLM rules require a configured LLM transport

claims.verifyVia: combination: `truecourse analyze --llm` with no transport configured surfaces the missing transport on stdout or a non-zero exit

claims.title: deterministic and LLM rules can each be toggled per repository

claims.verifyVia: combination: `truecourse rules` toggles change the repo's stored settings and the next analysis honors them

claims.title: a file over the per-file time budget is skipped with a warning

claims.verifyVia: stdout: a skip warning naming the offending file

claims.title: the analysis always completes and writes its output
claims.claim: Even when files are skipped for exceeding the per-file time budget, the analysis completes and writes its output.
claims.verifyVia: combination: exit code 0 plus the JSON results written under `.truecourse/` on a run that emitted skip warnings

claims.title: the per-file budget defaults to 30 seconds
claims.claim: The deterministic scan's per-file time budget defaults to 30 seconds.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: the skip warning or run output reflecting a 30s default when the env override is unset

claims.title: TRUECOURSE_DET_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS overrides the per-file budget
claims.claim: Setting `TRUECOURSE_DET_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS` (in milliseconds) overrides the deterministic scan's per-file time budget.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: with the variable set to a very small value, the run emits per-file skip warnings it does not emit at the default

claims.title: JavaScript and TypeScript are supported
claims.claim: Analysis supports JavaScript and TypeScript source files.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: violations reported against .js/.ts files in the analyzed repo

claims.title: Python is supported
claims.claim: Analysis supports Python source files.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: violations reported against .py files in the analyzed repo

claims.title: C# is supported with the .NET 8 SDK
claims.claim: Analysis supports C# source files when the .NET 8 SDK is available.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: violations reported against .cs files in the analyzed repo

claims.title: C# semantic rules need the Roslyn host built once

claims.title: analyzing C# without the Roslyn host fails fast

claims.verifyVia: combination: non-zero exit and an error on stdout/stderr naming the missing Roslyn host

claims.title: analyze prompts before stashing a dirty tree
claims.claim: Run on a dirty working tree, `truecourse analyze` prompts for confirmation before stashing pending changes.
claims.verifyVia: prompt: the stash confirmation appears before any analysis work

claims.title: --stash pre-approves stashing
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --stash` stashes pending changes without prompting, so the run is non-interactive in CI.
claims.verifyVia: combination: no prompt appears and the run completes with the working tree changes stashed

claims.title: --no-stash analyzes the working tree as-is
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --no-stash` analyzes the working tree as it stands, without stashing and without prompting.
claims.verifyVia: combination: no prompt appears, the uncommitted changes remain in the working tree, and the results reflect them

claims.title: --diff reports new and resolved violations from uncommitted changes
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --diff` reports the violations the uncommitted changes introduce and the ones they resolve.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: separate new and resolved violation sets attributable to the uncommitted edits

claims.title: --llm runs LLM rules in addition to deterministic ones
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --llm` runs the LLM rules in addition to the deterministic scan.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: the run reports LLM rule results / LLM usage alongside deterministic findings

claims.title: --llm pre-approves the cost estimate
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --llm` pre-approves the cost estimate, so the run proceeds without stopping at the cost confirmation prompt.
claims.verifyVia: prompt: no cost-estimate confirmation is presented, and the run proceeds to completion unattended

claims.title: --no-llm skips LLM rules for the run
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --no-llm` skips the LLM rules for that run.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: the run reports no LLM calls and no LLM-rule findings

claims.title: list --all shows all violations without pagination
claims.claim: `truecourse list --all` prints all violations with no pagination.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: the row count matches the analysis total and no pagination footer is printed

claims.title: list --severity filters by severity
claims.claim: `truecourse list --severity high,critical` prints only violations of the named severities.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: every printed row carries one of the requested severities

claims.title: add registers a repo without analyzing it
claims.claim: `truecourse add` registers the repository without running an analysis.
claims.verifyVia: combination: stdout confirms registration while no analysis results are written under `.truecourse/`

claims.title: the first analyze creates .truecourse/
claims.claim: The first `truecourse analyze` in a repository creates the `.truecourse/` directory in that repository.
claims.verifyVia: file: `.truecourse/` does not exist before the run and exists after it

claims.title: LATEST.json, config.json and hooks.yaml are committable
claims.claim: `LATEST.json`, `config.json` and `hooks.yaml` inside `.truecourse/` are committable, so git does not ignore them and they travel with the repo.
claims.verifyVia: file: git does not report these three paths as ignored (e.g. `git check-ignore` finds no match)

claims.title: LATEST.json holds the most recent analysis snapshot
claims.claim: `.truecourse/LATEST.json` holds the most recent analysis snapshot.
claims.verifyVia: file: `.truecourse/LATEST.json` exists after an analysis and its contents match that run's results

claims.title: LATEST.json doubles as the baseline for --diff and the pre-commit hook
claims.claim: `.truecourse/LATEST.json` doubles as the baseline that `truecourse analyze --diff` and the pre-commit hook compare against.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a diff run and a hook run both report deltas relative to the contents of the committed LATEST.json

claims.title: config.json holds per-repo rule categories and LLM toggles
claims.claim: `.truecourse/config.json` holds the per-repository rule categories and LLM toggles.
claims.verifyVia: file: category and LLM toggle changes are reflected in `.truecourse/config.json`

claims.title: hooks.yaml holds the pre-commit policy and is created by hooks install
claims.claim: `.truecourse/hooks.yaml` holds the pre-commit hook policy and is created by `truecourse hooks install`.
claims.verifyVia: file: `.truecourse/hooks.yaml` is absent before `hooks install` and present after it

claims.title: local-only store files are gitignored automatically
claims.claim: `analyses/`, `diff.json`, `history.json`, `ui-state.json`, `logs/` and `.analyze.lock` are local-only and are added to `.truecourse/.gitignore` automatically.
claims.verifyVia: file: `.truecourse/.gitignore` is created by TrueCourse and git reports each of these paths as ignored

claims.title: the documented baseline setup sequence works
claims.claim: After `truecourse analyze`, `git add .truecourse/LATEST.json .truecourse/config.json` succeeds and both files can be committed as the baseline.
claims.verifyVia: combination: `git add` exits 0 for both paths and `git status` shows them staged

claims.title: re-running analyze refreshes LATEST.json
claims.claim: Re-running `truecourse analyze` updates `.truecourse/LATEST.json` to the new snapshot, which is then committed to refresh the baseline.
claims.verifyVia: file: `.truecourse/LATEST.json` content changes after a second analysis over changed code

claims.title: analyze --diff reports new and resolved violations
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --diff` reports the new and the resolved violations produced by the uncommitted changes.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a violation added by the edits appears as new and one removed by them appears as resolved

claims.title: list --diff shows the diff results
claims.claim: `truecourse list --diff` prints the results of the last diff analysis.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: the rows match the preceding `analyze --diff` output rather than the full violation set

claims.title: --diff compares the working tree against the committed baseline
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --diff` compares the working tree against the committed baseline rather than against a fresh full analysis.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: the diff is computed against the committed LATEST.json even when no local full analysis was run in this checkout

claims.title: --diff reports only what the changes introduce or resolve
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --diff` reports only the violations the changes introduce and resolve, so violations already present in the baseline are not reported.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a known pre-existing baseline violation is absent from the diff output

claims.title: the diff result lands in .truecourse/diff.json
claims.claim: The result of `truecourse analyze --diff` is written to `.truecourse/diff.json`.
claims.verifyVia: file: `.truecourse/diff.json` exists after a diff run and matches the reported diff

claims.title: diff.json is per-checkout and overwritten each run
claims.claim: `.truecourse/diff.json` is overwritten by each diff run rather than accumulating history.
claims.verifyVia: file: after a second diff run over different edits, diff.json holds only the second run's result

claims.title: the pre-commit hook runs the same diff check
claims.claim: The pre-commit hook runs the same `analyze --diff` check on every commit.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: the hook output during `git commit` reports the same new/resolved violations as a manual `analyze --diff`

claims.title: worktrees and fresh clones inherit the baseline through git
claims.claim: Because `LATEST.json` is tracked, a new `git worktree add` checkout and a fresh clone both inherit the committed baseline through git.
claims.verifyVia: file: `.truecourse/LATEST.json` is present in a newly created worktree and in a fresh clone with no TrueCourse command run there

claims.title: analyze --diff works in a new worktree with no cold start
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --diff` works on the first commit in a new worktree with no per-checkout cold-start analysis, reporting what the in-flight changes introduce relative to the baseline committed on main.
claims.verifyVia: combination: in a freshly created worktree with no prior local analysis, `analyze --diff` exits 0 and reports the new violations of the in-flight edits

claims.title: the pre-commit hook works on the first commit in a new worktree
claims.claim: The pre-commit hook works on the first commit made in a new worktree, with no per-checkout cold-start analysis.
claims.verifyVia: combination: the first `git commit` in a fresh worktree triggers the hook's diff check and reaches a verdict

claims.title: a full analyze prompts before stashing a dirty tree
claims.claim: On a dirty working tree, a full `truecourse analyze` prompts before stashing the pending changes.
claims.verifyVia: prompt: the stash confirmation is shown before analysis begins

claims.title: --stash pre-approves stashing pending changes
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --stash` pre-approves stashing the pending changes, so the run needs no interactive answer.
claims.verifyVia: combination: no prompt is shown and the analysis proceeds with the changes stashed

claims.title: --no-stash analyzes the working tree as-is
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --no-stash` analyzes the working tree as-is and does not stash.
claims.verifyVia: combination: no prompt is shown and the uncommitted changes are still present in the working tree after the run

claims.title: rule configuration is per repository
claims.claim: Which rule categories and LLM-powered rules are enabled is configured per repository, so two repositories can carry different policies.
claims.verifyVia: combination: a toggle applied in one repo does not change the reported status in another repo

claims.title: rule configuration is stored in .truecourse/config.json

claims.title: rules categories shows enabled/disabled status

claims.verifyVia: stdout: one row per category with an on/off state

claims.verifyVia: combination: `rules categories` afterwards reports style as enabled and config.json records it

claims.title: rules categories --disable disables a category

claims.verifyVia: combination: `rules categories` afterwards reports style as disabled and config.json records it

claims.title: rules categories --reset restores the global default
claims.claim: `truecourse rules categories --reset` resets the repository's category selection to the global default.
claims.verifyVia: combination: after a disable followed by --reset, `rules categories` reports the default state again

claims.title: rules llm shows LLM rules status
claims.claim: `truecourse rules llm` prints whether LLM rules are enabled for the repository.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: the LLM rules status line

claims.title: rules llm --enable enables LLM rules
claims.claim: `truecourse rules llm --enable` enables LLM rules for the repository.
claims.verifyVia: combination: `rules llm` afterwards reports them enabled and config.json records it

claims.title: rules llm --disable disables LLM rules
claims.claim: `truecourse rules llm --disable` disables LLM rules for the repository.
claims.verifyVia: combination: `rules llm` afterwards reports them disabled and config.json records it

claims.title: analyze --llm runs LLM rules for that run and pre-approves the cost
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --llm` runs the LLM rules for that run and pre-approves the cost estimate.
claims.verifyVia: combination: no cost-estimate prompt appears and stdout reports LLM rule results

claims.title: analyze --no-llm skips LLM rules for that run only
claims.claim: `truecourse analyze --no-llm` skips the LLM rules for that run only, leaving the repository's persisted LLM setting unchanged.
claims.verifyVia: combination: the run reports no LLM results while `rules llm` afterwards still reports LLM rules enabled

claims.title: rules list lists rules with on/off status
claims.claim: `truecourse rules list` lists the individual rules with their on/off status.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: rule rows each carrying an enabled/disabled state

claims.title: rules list --disabled shows only disabled rules
claims.claim: `truecourse rules list --disabled` shows only the rules that are currently disabled.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: every listed rule is disabled, and a rule disabled beforehand appears

claims.title: rules list --domain restricts to one domain
claims.claim: `truecourse rules list --domain security` lists only the rules in the named domain.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: every listed rule belongs to the security domain

claims.title: rules list --search filters by key, name or description
claims.claim: `truecourse rules list --search sql` lists only rules whose key, name, or description matches the search term.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: every listed rule matches the term in one of those three fields

claims.title: rules list --language shows per-language support status
claims.claim: `truecourse rules list --language python` shows the rules' support status for the named language.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: rows carrying a per-language support indicator for Python

claims.title: rules disable turns off one rule
claims.claim: `truecourse rules disable <ruleKey>` disables that single rule for the repository.
claims.verifyVia: combination: `rules list --disabled` afterwards includes the key and config.json records it

claims.title: rules enable re-enables one rule
claims.claim: `truecourse rules enable <ruleKey>` re-enables a single previously disabled rule.
claims.verifyVia: combination: `rules list --disabled` afterwards omits the key and config.json no longer records it

claims.title: rules reset <ruleKey> clears one rule's override
claims.claim: `truecourse rules reset <ruleKey>` clears the per-rule override for that one rule.
claims.verifyVia: combination: the named rule returns to its default state while other overrides remain in config.json

claims.title: rules reset with no key clears every per-rule override
claims.claim: `truecourse rules reset` with no rule key clears all per-rule overrides.
claims.verifyVia: combination: after several disables, `rules list --disabled` is empty and config.json holds no per-rule overrides

claims.title: disabled rules are skipped at analyze time
claims.claim: A disabled rule is skipped at analyze time, so a later analysis produces no new violations from it.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: code that tripped the rule before disabling produces no violation of that rule after

claims.title: disabling a rule removes its detection and LLM cost
claims.claim: A disabled rule incurs no detection cost and, for an LLM rule, makes no LLM calls during analysis.

claims.title: existing violations from a disabled rule are hidden from list
claims.claim: Existing violations from a rule are hidden from `truecourse list` once that rule is disabled, without re-running the analysis.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: violations of the rule present in `truecourse list` before the disable are absent immediately afterwards

claims.title: re-enabling a rule restores its hidden violations
claims.claim: Violations hidden by disabling a rule reappear in `truecourse list` once the rule is re-enabled.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: the previously hidden violations are listed again after `rules enable <ruleKey>`

claims.title: disabled rule keys live under disabledRules in config.json
claims.claim: The keys of disabled rules are stored in `<repo>/.truecourse/config.json` under `disabledRules`.
claims.verifyVia: file: the disabled rule's key appears in the `disabledRules` array of config.json

claims.title: the pre-commit hook blocks commits introducing new violations
claims.claim: With the pre-commit hook installed, a commit that introduces a new violation at or above the configured severity is blocked.
claims.verifyVia: combination: `git commit` exits non-zero, prints the blocking violation, and no new commit exists

claims.title: hooks install installs the pre-commit hook
claims.claim: `truecourse hooks install` installs a pre-commit hook into the repository.
claims.verifyVia: combination: stdout confirms installation and a subsequent `git commit` triggers the hook

claims.title: hooks uninstall removes the pre-commit hook
claims.claim: `truecourse hooks uninstall` removes the installed pre-commit hook.
claims.verifyVia: combination: after uninstall, a commit that would have been blocked completes with no hook output

claims.title: hooks status shows hook status and configuration
claims.claim: `truecourse hooks status` prints whether the hook is installed along with its configuration.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: an installed/not-installed state plus the configured block severities

claims.title: the hook runs analyze --diff on every commit
claims.claim: On every commit the hook runs `truecourse analyze --diff` against the repository's last full analysis.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: each `git commit` emits diff-analysis output before the commit is created

claims.title: the hook blocks when a new violation matches the block severities
claims.claim: The hook blocks the commit when any newly-introduced violation matches the configured block severities.
claims.verifyVia: combination: non-zero exit from `git commit` naming the matching violation, and `git log` unchanged

claims.title: the hook lets through commits with no matching new violation

claims.title: the hook diffs against .truecourse/LATEST.json

claims.verifyVia: stdout: the hook reports the same new violations as a manual `analyze --diff` against the committed LATEST.json

claims.title: hooks install warns and requires confirmation

claims.title: declining the confirmation installs no hook

claims.title: git commit --no-verify bypasses the hook

claims.title: hooks install seeds hooks.yaml with starter defaults

claims.title: the hook reads its policy only from hooks.yaml

claims.title: a deleted hooks.yaml makes the hook warn

claims.title: a deleted hooks.yaml passes every commit

claims.title: the seeded block-on default is critical and high

claims.title: block-on accepts the five documented severities

claims.title: setting llm true runs LLM rules on every commit

claims.title: analyze honors .gitignore

claims.verifyVia: stdout: a violation-bearing file listed in .gitignore produces no violations in `truecourse list`

claims.title: nested .gitignore files are honored
claims.claim: Analysis honors nested `.gitignore` files, not just the one at the repository root.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a violation-bearing file excluded by a subdirectory .gitignore produces no violations

claims.title: .git/info/exclude is honored

claims.verifyVia: stdout: a violation-bearing file excluded only via .git/info/exclude produces no violations

claims.title: the configured global excludes file is honored

claims.title: .truecourseignore excludes tracked paths from analysis
claims.claim: A `.truecourseignore` at the repository root excludes the paths it matches from analysis even though git still tracks them.
claims.verifyVia: combination: the file remains tracked by git while its violations are absent from `truecourse list`

claims.title: .truecourseignore uses .gitignore syntax
claims.claim: `.truecourseignore` uses the same syntax as `.gitignore`, supporting `#` comment lines, directory patterns such as `src/generated/`, and specific file paths such as `scripts/ingest-epub.js`.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a .truecourseignore containing all three documented forms excludes exactly the intended files from `truecourse list`

claims.title: patterns are anchored to the file's location
claims.claim: Patterns are anchored to the location of the `.truecourseignore` file, so `src/generated/` matches only the top-level `src/generated` directory.
claims.verifyVia: stdout: a nested `lib/src/generated/` file is still analyzed while the top-level one is not

claims.title: **/ patterns match at any depth

claims.title: .truecourseignore also narrows spec scan doc discovery

claims.verifyVia: file: after `truecourse spec scan`, the excluded markdown path is absent from `.truecourse/specs/corpus.json`

claims.title: TRUECOURSE_ROSLYN_HOST points at a prebuilt C# Roslyn host binary

claims.title: TRUECOURSE_NO_PRICE_FETCH skips the model-price fetch

claims.verifyVia: combination: the run makes no price request and prices come from the bundled list

claims.title: TRUECOURSE_TELEMETRY=0 opts out of telemetry

claims.verifyVia: combination: no telemetry is sent while the variable is 0
